articles.title: US tech giants warn Europe that ditching US tech giants could cost €115B
articles.summary: A study commissioned by a US technology industry group estimates that European cloud sovereignty policies could impose €115 billion in costs over a decade. The findings reflect modeled scenarios rather than established costs, highlighting the competing arguments around digital independence, vendor choice, and the economics of cloud infrastructure.

articles.title: Internet traffic records topple as Champions League returns
articles.summary: European internet exchanges recorded major traffic spikes as Champions League matches resumed, with DE-CIX Frankfurt reaching a reported 21.47 Tbps. The new records demonstrate how live streaming continues to push network capacity, traffic engineering, and infrastructure resilience.

articles.title: SAP customers seek renewed control over their ERP fate
articles.summary: SAP customers are pushing back on cloud migration pressure, asking for more flexibility, predictable licensing, and continued support for hybrid and on-premises ERP deployments. With many organizations still running older SAP systems ahead of the 2027 support deadline, the debate highlights growing tensions between vendor roadmaps and enterprise technology strategies.

articles.title: The Rise of DeployCos
articles.summary: AI labs, hyperscalers, and incumbent consultancies are increasingly establishing specialized deployment companies—or DeployCos—to embed forward-deployed engineers directly inside enterprises. These entities help bridge the "diffusion gap" or "capability overhang" by assisting organizations with custom workflow integration, systems access, and organizational change management.

articles.title: Chasing that 32 ms tail latency in ClickHouse
articles.summary: Engineers at ClickHouse investigated why simple SELECT queries experienced an unexpected 32 ms tail latency after idle periods on high-RTT networks. They discovered that unbatched metadata packets sent alongside result data quickly exhausted the TCP congestion window after it had been reset to its initial size during idleness. To resolve the issue, ClickHouse implemented application-level batching for these metadata packets, effectively halving the TCP segment count and eliminating the tail latency penalty.

articles.title: Firefox takes aim at the enterprise browser market
articles.summary: Mozilla is introducing Firefox Enterprise with centralized policy management, security controls, and a self-hostable administration console. Initially targeting four European countries, the offering gives organizations another managed browser option, particularly those seeking more infrastructure control and less dependence on Chromium.

articles.title: Shopify Is Widening the Catalog Door to Personal Agents. The Sign-Off Stays Human
articles.summary: Shopify is expanding its catalog access to shopper-configured personal agents while keeping a mandatory human sign-off on every purchase. The company's new Agentic Storefronts provide merchants out-of-the-box access to tools like ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Gemini, allowing billions of products to be discovered and purchased directly through agent conversations.

articles.title: Workday makes Sana its interface, launches Agent Harness, decision, and work intelligence
articles.summary: Workday announced at Workday Rising that it has made Sana the primary front-door interface for its platform and launched Agent Harness to let enterprises build secure AI agents for finance and HR data. The company also introduced ambient agents like the Talent Acquisition Agent, Workday Decision Intelligence, and Workday Work Intelligence. CEO Aneel Bhusri stated that Workday is refounding itself around artificial intelligence with a startup mindset.

articles.title: SolarWinds launches Avior AI agents to automate network operations
articles.summary: SolarWinds has introduced Avior AI agents designed to investigate network issues, identify configuration drift, and assist with incident remediation across enterprise environments. The platform supports varying levels of automation, from human-approved actions to autonomous workflows with auditability and safeguards.

articles.title: Cisco, Nvidia team up to build fatter, faster pluggable
articles.summary: Cisco and Nvidia have proposed a new optical transceiver form factor capable of supporting up to 12.8 Tbps of bandwidth. The design promises higher density and improved power efficiency for future data center networks, although commercial deployments remain ahead.

articles.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
articles.summary: To handle massive scaling challenges caused by AI-generated code that merged 30,000 changes daily, Anthropic built an in-house version control system called Scion and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. The company designed Scion around the assumption that clients are always online, implementing a centralized server architecture, horizontal scalability, server-side commits, and sparse checkouts. This new infrastructure reduced CPU and memory requirements by 200x compared to their previous git mirroring setup and accelerated CI code checkouts from minutes to seconds.

articles.title: Ultra Ethernet 1.1 extends the specification to scale-up networks and adds programmable congestion control
articles.summary: The latest Ultra Ethernet specification introduces networking improvements designed to support larger computing clusters and more sophisticated congestion management.

articles.title: Developer guide to Gemini 4 Argon Long Decode
articles.summary: Google has introduced Long Decode for the Gemini 4 Argon model, enabling completions up to 1 million tokens long by splitting generation across multiple model inferences.
